narrative.title: Dialing Through the Call Center's Vanity Codes
narrative.scenario: A call center reserves vanity extensions typed as digit strings, and the switchboard must publish every word each digit sequence could spell under the classic keypad mapping (2 = ABC, 3 = DEF, and so on; 7 and 9 carry four letters). The operator types one digit at a time, branching over that key's letters, and the catalogue is complete when the last digit's options are exhausted.
narrative.inputFormat: A string digits containing only characters '2'-'9'.
narrative.outputFormat: Every letter combination, in the order the depth-first walk produces them; an empty input yields an empty list.
constraints: digits[i] is a digit in the range ['2', '9']

complexity.optimalTime: O(4^n * n) worst case — up to 4 letters per digit, n to copy each string
complexity.optimalSpace: O(n) recursion depth beyond the output

testCases.explanation: Three letters for '2' times three for '3', crossed in keypad order.
A single digit simply lists its own letters.

hintLevels: Level 1: This is a word-by-word expansion — each digit opens as many branches as it has letters.
Level 2: Keep a keypad table; at depth d, loop over table[digits[d]], append each letter, recurse to d + 1, and pop it back off.
Level 3: Guard the empty input before recursing — otherwise the base case fires immediately and emits one empty string instead of nothing.
